templates: The protein is located in the {label}.
This protein can be found in the {label}.
Within the cell, the protein is found in the {label}.
The protein is localized in the {label}.
deeploc.meta_prompt:
Generate exactly 5 diverse, natural-language sentence templates that a biologist would use to describe where a protein is located within a cell.

Each template must contain the placeholder {label} exactly once -- not zero times, not two or more times. {label} will be substituted, one at a time, with each of these exact labels: 'nucleus', 'cytoplasm', 'extracellular space', 'mitochondrion', 'cell membrane', 'endoplasmic reticulum', 'chloroplast', 'Golgi apparatus', 'lysosome or vacuole', 'peroxisome'. Every one of your 5 templates must read as a grammatically correct, natural sentence for every single one of these labels -- check each one before finalizing your answer.

Critically, all 5 templates must express exactly the same underlying biological claim -- vary ONLY the wording and sentence structure, never the meaning. Do not let any one template imply a different degree of certainty, causality, directness, or scope than the others (for example, a phrase implying indirect or partial involvement, like 'contributes to', is a different, weaker claim than direct possession, like 'has' or 'is capable of' -- do not mix claim types like this across the 5 templates). The 5 templates must be interchangeable paraphrases of ONE fixed statement, not 5 different statements.

Keep the sentences plain and simple, similar in style and structure to each other -- straightforward statements, not elaborate or abstract phrasing. Do not reference specific experimental methods (e.g. microscopy, immunofluorescence staining, biochemical assays) or phrase it as reporting an experimental finding -- state the fact directly. Avoid database-specific jargon or fixed field-style formatting (e.g. do not write 'Subcellular location: {label}.'). Return your answer as a JSON array of exactly 5 strings, nothing else -- no markdown, no numbering, no explanation.

2026-08-15d: manually hand-patched template #4 ("The protein's location within the cell is the {label}." -> "The protein is localized in the {label}."), before any evaluation was run. The old wording semantically conflicts with the 'extracellular space' label: 'within the cell' and 'extracellular' (outside the cell) contradict each other -- "The protein's location within the cell is the extracellular space" is a self-contradictory sentence, not merely awkward. The other 4 templates were left unchanged. Not a performance-based edit.

revisions: 2026-08-15: template #5 ("This enzyme is grouped within the {label} class.") hand-patched to "This enzyme is grouped among the {label}." before any evaluation was run. As generated, {label} appeared adjectivally before "class", which grammatically demands the singular enzyme name ("the hydrolase class"), while {label} is always filled with the plural canonical class name from CLASSES ("Hydrolases", also used for Label-only/confusion-matrix) -- 'the Hydrolases class' is ungrammatical. The other 4 templates use {label} as a plural object/head noun ('one of the {label}', 'a member of the {label}'), which the plural form fits correctly. Verified by filling all 7 classes into all 5 templates and reading each sentence before and after the fix. A grammar fix caught pre-evaluation, not a performance-based edit -- same discipline as the DeepLoc revision note in generate_zero_shot_prompt_templates.py.

Done before any evaluation was run against these templates -- not based on classification results. See generate_zero_shot_prompt_templates.py's module docstring for the full rationale.

2026-08-15c: the SAME adjectival-{label}-before-'class' grammar bug from the 2026-08-15 fix reappeared in the 2026-08-15b regeneration, in a different template slot -- template #3, "This enzyme is a member of the {label} class.", produces "the hydrolases class" (ungrammatical; wants the singular "hydrolase") for the identical reason as before. The new meta-prompt's 'check every label' instruction did not prevent this recurrence -- Claude generated the same pre-nominal-modifier + 'class' pattern again despite the explicit per-label grammar check. Hand-patched by dropping 'class' ("This enzyme is a member of the {label}."), matching the plural-object pattern already used by 3 of the other 4 templates. Caught by re-running the same fill-every-label verification used throughout this file, before any evaluation was run. Not a performance-based edit -- and not re-sent to the API, since no new templates were generated (a one-word deletion), consistent with 'exactly one new API call per task' already being satisfied by the 2026-08-15b regeneration.

2026-08-15d: manually replaced template #3 ("This enzyme falls under the broad category of {label}.") and template #5 ("This enzyme is categorized as a type of {label}.") with "This enzyme belongs to the group of {label}." and "This enzyme is classified among the {label}." respectively, before any evaluation was run. The two replaced templates read as more administrative/database-classification phrasing ("falls under the broad category of", "is categorized as a type of") than the other three, which state direct class membership plainly -- the fix keeps all 5 templates semantically and stylistically closer to a single 'this enzyme is a member of {label}' claim, matching the same-underlying-claim requirement more consistently than the 2026-08-15b regeneration did on its own. Verified by filling all 7 EC labels into all 5 templates and reading each sentence. Not a performance-based edit; no new API call was made.

go_mf.meta_prompt:
Generate exactly 5 diverse, natural-language sentence templates that a biologist would use to describe a protein's molecular function. Note that a protein can have more than one molecular function, so avoid templates implying this is its only or defining function (e.g. avoid "This protein's sole function is {label}.").

Each template must contain the placeholder {label} exactly once -- not zero times, not two or more times. {label} will be substituted, one at a time, with each of these exact labels: 'hydrolase activity', 'transcription regulator activity', 'molecular transducer activity', 'molecular function regulator activity', 'DNA binding', 'transporter activity', 'transferase activity', 'cytoskeletal protein binding', 'RNA binding', 'receptor ligand activity'. Every one of your 5 templates must read as a grammatically correct, natural sentence for every single one of these labels -- check each one before finalizing your answer.

Critically, all 5 templates must express exactly the same underlying biological claim -- vary ONLY the wording and sentence structure, never the meaning. Do not let any one template imply a different degree of certainty, causality, directness, or scope than the others (for example, a phrase implying indirect or partial involvement, like 'contributes to', is a different, weaker claim than direct possession, like 'has' or 'is capable of' -- do not mix claim types like this across the 5 templates). The 5 templates must be interchangeable paraphrases of ONE fixed statement, not 5 different statements. In particular, do NOT use 'contributes to {label}' or any similar phrasing implying indirect or partial involvement -- every template must state that the protein directly has or performs the molecular function, with the same directness throughout.

Keep the sentences plain and simple, similar in style and structure to each other -- straightforward statements, not elaborate or abstract phrasing. Do not reference specific experimental methods (e.g. microscopy, immunofluorescence staining, biochemical assays) or phrase it as reporting an experimental finding -- state the fact directly.
